title: From Zoonotic Spillover to Hemorrhagic Crisis: Molecular Insights and Epidemiology of Ethiopia’s 2025 Marburg Outbreak Amid Preparedness Gaps and Historical Lethality
abstract: Ethiopia confirmed its first Marburg virus disease (MVD) outbreak on 14 November 2025 in Jinka (Omo Valley area), where a single spillover from Rousettus aegyptiacus resulted in nine laboratory-confirmed cases and eight deaths (CFR 89%). Transmission occurred in the context of concurrent cholera and large-scale population displacement. Despite these pressures, case confirmation was achieved within 48 hours, >90% of contacts were traced, and same-day L-gene sequencing placed the isolate within the East African lineage associated with the 2024 Rwanda outbreak. This review summarizes key molecular determinants of MARV virulence including GP–NPC1 mediated entry, VP24-driven interferon antagonism, and GP-associated endothelial dysfunction and examines Ethiopia’s contrasting strengths in genomic capacity and PHEOC coordination versus persistent constraints in diagnostics, clinical readiness, and countermeasure access. We outline a feasible seven-day containment framework integrating low-cost molecular testing, remdesivir therapy, and VSV-MARV ring vaccination to prevent further spread in resource-limited settings.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines Marburg virus disease (MVD) in Ethiopia, focusing on the 2025 outbreak in Jinka (Omo Valley), its zoonotic spillover from Rousettus aegyptiacus, and subsequent human-to-human transmission dynamics. It addresses the central question of how molecular determinants of Marburg virus (MARV) virulence intersect with Ethiopia’s public health system preparedness and response gaps during concurrent cholera outbreaks and population displacement.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis summarizing molecular determinants of MARV virulence and Ethiopia’s outbreak response. It describes Ethiopia’s genomic sequencing capacity, PHEOC coordination, and diagnostic/clinical constraints without specifying databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria. The review does not report a systematic search, meta-analysis, or explicit consensus process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review identifies key molecular determinants of MARV virulence, including GP–NPC1 mediated viral entry, VP24-driven interferon antagonism, and GP-associated endothelial dysfunction. It highlights Ethiopia’s rapid case confirmation (<48 hours), high contact tracing coverage (>90%), and genomic sequencing linking the outbreak to the 2024 Rwanda lineage. The review also notes the outbreak’s high case fatality rate (89%) and concurrent public health pressures.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights persistent gaps in Ethiopia’s diagnostic capacity, clinical readiness, and access to countermeasures despite strengths in genomic sequencing and PHEOC coordination. It does not resolve conflicting findings or address unresolved mechanisms, as no comparative or experimental data are presented. The review also does not evaluate heterogeneity in transmission dynamics or host susceptibility.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes a seven-day containment framework integrating low-cost molecular testing, remdesivir therapy, and VSV-MARV ring vaccination to mitigate spread in resource-limited settings. It emphasizes the need for scalable diagnostics and clinical protocols tailored to concurrent outbreaks, though these recommendations are not grounded in empirical evaluation.

analysis.summary_en: This review synthesizes Ethiopia’s 2025 Marburg virus disease (MVD) outbreak, tracing its zoonotic spillover from Rousettus aegyptiacus to nine confirmed cases and eight deaths (CFR 89%) in Jinka. The review highlights rapid genomic confirmation (<48 hours), high contact tracing (>90%), and linkage to the 2024 Rwanda lineage, but underscores persistent gaps in diagnostics, clinical readiness, and countermeasure access. It proposes a seven-day containment framework combining low-cost molecular testing, remdesivir, and ring vaccination for resource-limited settings.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述对埃塞俄比亚的马尔堡病毒病 (MVD) 进行了研究,重点关注 2025 年金卡(奥莫河谷)的疫情、埃及白蚁的人畜共患病溢出以及随后的人际传播动态。它解决了马尔堡病毒(MARV)毒力的分子决定因素如何与埃塞俄比亚公共卫生系统的准备工作和霍乱同时爆发和人口流离失所期间的应对差距相互交叉的核心问题。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一篇叙述性综合文章,总结了 MARV 毒力的分子决定因素和埃塞俄比亚的疫情应对措施。它描述了埃塞俄比亚的基因组测序能力、公共卫生紧急行动中心协调以及诊断/临床限制,但没有具体说明数据库、搜索日期或资格标准。该综述没有报告系统搜索、荟萃分析或明确的共识过程。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述确定了 MARV 毒力的关键分子决定因素,包括 GP-NPC1 介导的病毒进入、VP24 驱动的干扰素拮抗作用和 GP 相关的内皮功能障碍。它强调了埃塞俄比亚的快速病例确认(<48 小时)、高接触者追踪覆盖率(>90%)以及将疫情与 2024 年卢旺达血统联系起来的基因组测序。审查还指出了此次疫情的高病死率(89%)和同时存在的公共卫生压力。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查强调了埃塞俄比亚在基因组测序和公共卫生紧急行动中心协调方面的优势,但在诊断能力、临床准备和获得对策方面持续存在差距。它没有解决相互矛盾的发现或解决未解决的机制,因为没有提供比较或实验数据。该综述也没有评估传播动力学或宿主易感性的异质性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查提出了一个为期 7 天的遏制框架,整合了低成本分子检测、瑞德西韦治疗和 VSV-MARV 环疫苗接种,以减轻资源有限环境中的传播。它强调需要针对同时爆发的可扩展诊断和临床方案,尽管这些建议并非基于经验评估。

abstract_zh: 埃塞俄比亚于 2025 年 11 月 14 日在金卡(奥莫河谷地区)确认了首例马尔堡病毒病 (MVD) 疫情,其中一次埃及白粉菌的溢出导致 9 例实验室确诊病例和 8 例死亡(病死率 89%)。传播是在霍乱和大规模人口流离失所同时发生的情况下发生的。尽管面临这些压力,我们还是在 48 小时内完成了病例确认,追踪了超过 90% 的接触者,并且当天的 L 基因测序将该分离株归入与 2024 年卢旺达疫情相关的东非谱系。本综述总结了 MARV 毒力的关键分子决定因素,包括 GP-NPC1 介导的进入、VP24 驱动的干扰素拮抗作用和 GP 相关的内皮功能障碍,并研究了埃塞俄比亚在基因组能力和公共卫生紧急事件协调方面的对比优势与诊断、临床准备和对策获取方面的持续限制。我们概述了一个可行的 7 天遏制框架,整合了低成本分子检测、瑞德西韦治疗和 VSV-MARV 环疫苗接种,以防止资源有限的环境中进一步传播。

title: Digital Health for Pandemic Preparedness: A Critical Review of Innovations, Equity Gaps, and Governance in Infectious Disease Surveillance
abstract: Context: Recent infectious disease emergencies, including SARS-CoV-2, mpox (2022 - 2024), highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in US dairy cattle (2024 - 2025), and the Marburg virus in Rwanda (2024), have strained traditional surveillance systems. Digital health has been proposed as a paradigm shift; however, most reviews have focused on diagnostic accuracy while neglecting equity and governance. Evidence Acquisition: We conducted a structured thematic narrative review of peer-reviewed and grey literature published from January 2010 to March 2025, reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from February 5 to 18, 2025. Search keywords combined three concept blocks: (1) Digital-health technologies (artificial intelligence, machine learning, mHealth, eHealth, telemedicine, electronic health records, wearables, wastewater surveillance, genomic surveillance, natural-language processing); (2) infectious diseases (outbreak, pandemic, epidemic, COVID-19, Ebola, Zika, mpox, influenza, antimicrobial resistance, Marburg); and (3) public-health functions (surveillance, detection, forecasting, contact tracing, governance, equity). Full Boolean syntax is provided. Records were deduplicated in EndNote X20 and screened by 2 blinded reviewers in Rayyan (Cohen κ = 0.81). Empirical studies were appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool 2018, and reviews were appraised using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. The synthesis followed Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis and was interpreted through sociotechnical systems and data justice lenses. Results: Of 1498 records, 142 studies met the inclusion criteria; 48% (69/142) were rated as high quality. The evidence base was heavily skewed regionally (high-income countries [HICs], 41%; sub-Saharan Africa or South Asia, 19%). No technology was universally superior. Artificial intelligence (AI) studies were concentrated in HICs (18/32, 56%), whereas short-message-service (SMS) mHealth studies were concentrated in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs; 15/25, 60%). Recurring barriers included algorithmic bias, fragmented interoperability, donor-dependent sustainability, and slow benefit-sharing of pathogen data with LMICs. Conclusions: Across 142 included studies the synthesis supports a measured conclusion: Digital health is necessary but not sufficient for pandemic preparedness. The patterns most consistently observed in the evidence — regional skew, recurring governance failures, donor-dependent sustainability, and design choices that determine equity outcomes — together indicate that equity, sustainability, and accountability are constituents of effectiveness rather than obstacles to it. The binding constraint is increasingly political and institutional will rather than analytic uncertainty.

abstract_zh: 背景:近期的传染病突发事件,包括SARS-CoV-2、2022-2024年的猴痘(mpox)、2024-2025年美国奶牛中高致病性禽流感A(H5N1)以及2024年卢旺达马尔堡病毒疫情,已令传统监测系统不堪重负。数字健康被视为范式转变的方案;然而,大多数综述关注诊断准确性而忽视了公平性与治理问题。证据获取:本研究采用结构化主题叙事综述方法,纳入2010年1月至2025年3月发表的同行评审与灰色文献,报告遵循PRISMA 2020与PRISMA-ScR指南。于2025年2月5日至18日期间,在PubMed、Scopus与Web of Science数据库中进行检索。检索关键词由三个概念块组合而成:(1)数字健康技术(人工智能、机器学习、移动健康、电子健康、远程医疗、电子健康记录、可穿戴设备、污水监测、基因组监测、自然语言处理);(2)传染病(突发、大流行、流行、COVID-19、埃博拉、寨卡、猴痘、流感、抗菌素耐药性、马尔堡病毒);(3)公共卫生功能(监测、检测、预测、接触者追踪、治理、公平性)。完整布尔语法已提供。在EndNote X20中去重后,使用Rayyan平台由两名盲评审员筛选(Cohen κ=0.81)。实证研究采用《混合方法评估工具2018》进行质量评估,综述则采用Joanna Briggs研究所清单。综合分析遵循Braun与Clarke的反思性主题分析,并通过社会技术系统与数据正义视角进行解读。结果:共1498条记录中,142项研究符合纳入标准;其中69/142(48%)被评为高质量。证据库在地域分布上严重倾斜(高收入国家占41%,撒哈拉以南非洲或南亚占19%)。未发现任何技术具有普遍优越性。人工智能(AI)研究主要集中在高收入国家(32项中的18项,56%),而短信(SMS)移动健康研究则主要集中在中低收入国家(LMICs;25项中的15项,60%)。反复出现的障碍包括算法偏见、碎片化互操作性、捐助者依赖的可持续性以及病原体数据向LMICs的惠益分享缓慢。结论:在纳入的142项研究中,综合分析支持以下结论:数字健康对于大流行防备是必要但不充分的。证据中最一致观察到的模式——地域倾斜、反复出现的治理失败、捐助者依赖的可持续性以及决定公平性结果的设计选择——共同表明,公平性、可持续性与问责制是有效性的组成部分而非障碍。根本制约因素日益转向政治与制度意愿而非分析不确定性。
